📌 Watch-Only Wallets: Tracking Crypto Without Access to Funds

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

The Red Wave in Reverse: America Delivers a Stunning Rebuke to Trump 👏


Trump has suffered one of the most consequential political setbacks of his presidency, as voters across the United States delivered a sweeping victory to Democrats in the 2026 midterm elections. 

In a stunning reversal of the political landscape established by Trump’s 2024 victory, Democrats made major gains in Congress and scored historic wins in states long considered Republican strongholds. 

The results sent a clear message to the White House: the president’s political influence is no longer enough to guarantee victories for his party. The backlash was fueled by growing frustration over the cost of living, economic uncertainty and the administration’s controversial policies. 

Trump’s decision to place himself at the center of the midterm campaign turned the election into a nationwide judgment on his leadership. He repeatedly urged supporters to treat the contests as a referendum on his presidency. 

Millions of voters appeared to take that message seriously — but not in the way Republicans had hoped. Democrats capitalized on concerns about rising prices, tariffs and the war with Iran. Economic dissatisfaction proved particularly damaging, with voters increasingly questioning whether the administration had delivered on its promises to make life more affordable. 

The election also exposed cracks in the coalition that carried Trump back to the White House. Younger voters and Hispanic Americans showed signs of moving toward Democrats, weakening Republican support among groups the party had worked hard to attract. Some of the most dramatic results came from traditionally conservative states. 

Democratic victories in Texas and South Carolina demonstrated that even deeply entrenched Republican political advantages could be overcome. The party also made significant gains in other competitive states, putting control of Congress within its reach.For Republicans, the defeats represent more than a difficult election night. 

A Democratic majority would give the opposition powerful tools to challenge the administration, investigate its decisions and block key appointments. Congressional committees could become platforms for sustained scrutiny of Trump’s policies and the conduct of his administration. 

The political consequences may extend well beyond Capitol Hill. With the 2028 presidential race already looming on the horizon, the results raise serious questions about the Republican Party’s ability to maintain its electoral coalition. 

Trump’s influence remains considerable, but Tuesday’s results suggest that personal loyalty to the president cannot always overcome economic anxiety and voter dissatisfaction.

Democrats, meanwhile, have a major opportunity — but also a significant challenge. Winning an election by opposing Trump is one thing. Building a durable governing agenda that addresses voters’ everyday concerns is another. 

Their next moves will determine whether this historic breakthrough becomes the beginning of a broader political realignment or simply a powerful midterm backlash. 

One thing is unmistakable: American voters have dramatically changed the political equation in Washington. And Trump now faces a Congress far less willing to follow his lead.

⚠️ Tether leads $15M funding for Mural to power AI agent payments 

👀 Tether has led a $15 million Series A funding round for New York-based Mural, supporting the financial technology company’s development of payment infrastructure for businesses and artificial intelligence agents. Mural plans to use the investment to expand internationally and develop the banking, payment and compliance services needed for software agents to conduct financial transactions.

🔔 Founded in 2022 by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes, the company provides infrastructure that businesses use to manage accounts, payment instructions, identity verification and regulatory requirements across banking networks and blockchains. Its customers include global payroll provider Deel, browser developer Opera and financial technology platform Axexo. Through Mural’s system, businesses can offer accounts holding dollars, local currencies and stablecoins without managing separate financial infrastructure for each payment method.

📌 The company reported processing $2.1 billion in payments for users across 128 countries since introducing its application programming interface in 2025. Payment volume recorded so far in 2026 is nearly six times its total for 2025. Mural has not disclosed the valuation attached to the latest funding round. Fortune reported that the company previously raised $5 million in seed financing in 2022, followed by additional capital from existing backers.
